regulatory_floor_note: Dietary supplements are legally governed by an adult-oriented framework: FDA DSHEA sets no heavy-metal maxima; USP <2232> computes elemental-contaminant PDEs for an adult consumer; the food-supplement maximum levels several governments set (EU, GSO, Israel, Vietnam, Thailand, ASEAN, Singapore) are lax (lead 1000-10000, cadmium 300-1000, mercury 100-500 ug/kg). HMTc holds every supplement, adult- or child-labeled, to the strictest sovereign infant-and-child-food maximum level (Ages 0-5) by choice. The adult floor is disclosed on every cell and never selects the number.

Pb.analog_label: AU-NZ Standard 1.4.1 infant-formula lead maximum (the strictest sovereign infant lead ML)
Pb.label: Child-protective read-across from the strictest sovereign infant-and-child-food lead maximum (AU-NZ infant formula, 10 µg/kg). Adult supplement floors run 1000-10000 µg/kg (Thailand 1000; GSO/Israel/Vietnam 3000; ASEAN/Singapore 10000) and adult USP <2232> permits 5 µg/day (500 µg/kg at 10 g/day); California's developmental lead MADL is 0.5 µg/day. HMTc holds ALL supplements to 10 µg/kg because children consume adult supplements and lead has no threshold.
Pb.basis_note: child-protective read-across (voluntary over-compliance; adult floor disclosed, never selected)

iAs.analog_label: EU 2023/915 infant-formula inorganic-arsenic maximum (the strictest sovereign infant iAs ML)
iAs.analog_scope: infant formulae, follow-on formulae, food for special medical purposes intended for infants and young children, and young-child formulae placed on the market as liquid
iAs.label: Child-protective read-across from the strictest sovereign infant-and-child-food inorganic-arsenic maximum (EU infant formula, 10 µg/kg). No government sets an inorganic-arsenic supplement ML; adult USP <2232> permits inorganic arsenic 15 µg/day (1500 µg/kg at 10 g/day). HMTc holds ALL supplements to 10 µg/kg inorganic arsenic — 150x below the adult USP concentration floor. Basis disclosure: this EU anchor (source_id eu2023_ias_formula_liquid_10) is set on a liquid, as-consumed basis and is read across to the as-sold solid supplement WITHOUT a reconstitution adjustment. A reconstituted liquid formula is roughly 6-8x more dilute than the equivalent as-sold powder, so applying the liquid value directly to a solid is an intentional, disclosed over-strictness (the solid cell runs ~6-8x stricter than the equivalent as-sold powder ML), never an accidental wet/dry conflation; no serving-size conversion selects the limit.
iAs.basis_note: child-protective read-across (voluntary over-compliance; adult floor disclosed, never selected)

tAs.label: Child-protective read-across from the strictest sovereign infant-and-child-food total-arsenic maximum (India infant foods, 50 µg/kg). Total arsenic gates the inorganic-arsenic reflex; the toxic species iAs is anchored separately at 10 µg/kg. Adult supplement floors run 300-5000 µg/kg. HMTc holds ALL supplements to 50 µg/kg total arsenic.

MeHg.control: Total mercury is measured on every lot and bounds the methylmercury fraction (MeHg <= tHg). Reflex methylmercury speciation is required when the formulation contains marine-derived ingredients (fish, algae, seaweed, marine collagen, marine oil) or when total mercury approaches the child-protective ceiling. No government sets a supplement methylmercury limit below the binding total-mercury read-across.
MeHg.reference_method: Total Hg by EPA 7473 or ICP-MS; MeHg by species-specific GC-ICP-MS / HPLC-ICP-MS on marine-containing or elevated-tHg lots.

Cr-VI.control: Hexavalent chromium reduces to Cr(III) in a reducing supplement matrix and carries no stable burden; it is bounded by total chromium, measured on every lot. Any total-Cr result at or above 100 µg/kg triggers Cr(VI) speciation, and any quantifiable Cr(VI) fails certification. California lists Cr(VI) under Proposition 65 (oral MADL 8.2 µg/day) but sets no food concentration limit.
Cr-VI.reference_method: Total Cr by ICP-MS; Cr(VI) by EPA 3060A alkaline extraction with IC-ICP-MS (EPA 6800 / EN 15192) on a total-Cr exceedance; LOQ-level quantifiable Cr(VI) = fail.

Ni.label: Child-protective read-across from the strictest sovereign infant-and-child-food nickel maximum (EU liquid infant/young-child formula, 100 µg/kg). No government sets a nickel supplement ML and adult USP <2232> sets none; the entire adult framework is silent on supplement nickel, a metal EFSA reports European diets already exceed the tolerable intake for, children most of all. HMTc holds ALL supplements to 100 µg/kg. Basis disclosure: this EU anchor (source_id eu2024_ni_formula_liquid_100) is set on a liquid, as-consumed basis and is read across to the as-sold solid supplement WITHOUT a reconstitution adjustment. Sn.analog_label: India FSSAI infant-food tin maximum (the only non-canned infant tin ML on the register)
Sn.analog_scope: Infant Milk substitute and Infant foods
Sn.label: Child-protective read-across from the India FSSAI non-canned infant-food tin maximum (5000 µg/kg). Tin is a can-migration analyte; a non-canned supplement has no intrinsic tin source, so any quantifiable tin triggers a packaging investigation. No adult supplement tin ML exists. HMTc holds ALL supplements to 5000 µg/kg.

Al.label: Child-protective read-across from the AU-NZ non-soy infant-formula aluminium maximum (500 µg/kg) — the only government aluminium ML for any food in any jurisdiction. No adult supplement aluminium ML exists and USP <2232> sets none. HMTc holds ALL supplements to 500 µg/kg.

Cr.control: No government sets a total-chromium maximum level for any infant-and-child food, so no child-protective numeric anchor exists and none is invented. Total chromium is measured on every lot as a mandatory surveillance control and gates the hexavalent-chromium reflex. Cr(III) is nutritionally essential; the toxic species is Cr(VI), controlled separately. No adult supplement total-chromium ML exists.
Cr.reference_method: Total Cr by ICP-MS after microwave acid digestion.
